title: Citation Support Checklist
summary: Check that every citation resolves, identifies the intended source, and supports the nearby claim without scope, date, or attribution drift.
prerequisites: A draft containing citations or source links

sections.title: Check resolution, identity, entailment, and placement
paragraphs: First confirm the link resolves to the intended source and is not a search page, unrelated redirect, or fabricated address. Then confirm title, author or publisher, version, and date. Next read the cited passage and ask whether it directly supports the exact nearby claim. Finally, place the citation where a reader can tell which sentence it supports.

Watch for scope drift: a source about one model, plan, jurisdiction, benchmark, date, or population cannot silently support all others. A source that reports an association does not prove causation. A provider feature page does not establish independent comparative superiority.

Use five semantic support labels. DIRECT means the passage establishes the complete atomic claim within its stated scope. PARTIAL means it establishes only part of the claim or requires a material qualification. BACKGROUND means it supplies relevant context but does not establish the claim. UNSUPPORTED means the available evidence does not establish the proposition, including when the outcome was not measured or causation was not identified. CONTRADICTS requires an explicit opposing fact or conclusion. A statement that a quantity was not measured does not prove that an asserted value is false, so it is UNSUPPORTED rather than CONTRADICTS.

Split compound sentences before assigning support. One part can be DIRECT while another is UNSUPPORTED. Keep resolution, identity, semantic support, scope, and placement as separate decisions. A source can resolve correctly and still fail to support the claim.

sections.title: Run a claim-level citation audit
paragraphs: Treat model-generated citations as unverified suggestions until you open them. Do not grant an agent permission to access restricted systems merely to make a citation look complete.

Complete one row for each atomic material claim. Reusing an evidence ID is legitimate when one source supports multiple claims. Do not reuse a claim ID for different propositions. Write UNKNOWN for identity, scope, measurements, or conclusions that the accessible evidence does not establish.

code.label: Citation audit row
code.code:
Claim ID: [C-001]
Citation: [URL OR SAFE SOURCE ID]
Resolves: [YES | NO | PARTIAL]
Identity matches: [TITLE, PUBLISHER, VERSION, DATE]
Supporting passage: [SAFE QUOTE LOCATION OR SECTION]
Support strength: [DIRECT | PARTIAL | BACKGROUND | UNSUPPORTED | CONTRADICTS]
Scope matches: [YES | QUALIFICATION NEEDED | NO]
Placement unambiguous: [YES | NO]
Accessible alternative: [HTML OR TEXT AVAILABLE]
Action: [KEEP | REPLACE | QUALIFY | REMOVE]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is an audit row for every material citation, with a resolvable source, matching identity, located supporting passage, scope decision, and corrective action.

Open links in a clean session, verify access without relying on cached snippets, compare the source passage with the full claim, and recheck numerical and temporal qualifiers. Sample low-risk citations and inspect every high-consequence citation. Preserve an accessible text alternative when the source format is difficult to use.

If a source is missing or inaccessible, record which fields remain UNKNOWN and limit publication to accessible evidence. Do not seek unauthorized access. If accessible sources report genuinely conflicting facts, preserve both identities and passages, label the conflict, and report the disputed proposition as UNKNOWN unless a documented resolution establishes which evidence applies.

sections.title: Worked case: inspect the draft and evidence
paragraphs: This case is wholly synthetic. E-01 through E-05 are stable evidence IDs inside this exercise, not real URLs or publications. The report is titled "Study of Helpdesk Drafting Tools," published by the synthetic Helpdesk Methods Group, version 1.2, dated 2026-08-15. Its scope is 24 volunteer support agents, 12 per tool, in one 30-minute training exercise measuring whether each first draft met all 10 rubric requirements. It did not test production incidents, customer satisfaction, long-term outcomes, other populations, or other tools.

E-01 identity: "Study of Helpdesk Drafting Tools," Helpdesk Methods Group, version 1.2, 2026-08-15. Excerpt: "Among 12 Tool A participants, 9 first drafts met all 10 rubric requirements. Among 12 Tool B participants, 6 first drafts met all 10 rubric requirements. The exercise was conducted once with volunteers in a training environment."

E-02 identity: "Study of Helpdesk Drafting Tools," Helpdesk Methods Group, version 1.2, 2026-08-15. Excerpt: "The Tool A group had a higher pass proportion than the Tool B group in this exercise. Because participants were volunteers and were not randomly assigned, this result does not establish that Tool A caused the difference."

E-03 identity: "Study of Helpdesk Drafting Tools," Helpdesk Methods Group, version 1.2, 2026-08-15. Excerpt: "The association between prior drafting experience and passing was not estimated. The report contains no result for production customer satisfaction, no comparison with Tool C, and no result for the number of organizations using any tool."

E-04 identity: "Tool A quick-start page," Tool A publisher, version UNKNOWN, date UNKNOWN. Excerpt: "Tool A can create a first draft from a prompt." Only this copied plain-text fragment is available. The original page is inaccessible, so its current wording, version, date, and full scope cannot be verified.

E-05 identity: "Study of Helpdesk Drafting Tools," Helpdesk Methods Group, version 1.2, 2026-08-15. Excerpt: "For this exercise, a passing first draft met all 10 locally defined rubric requirements. The report did not evaluate whether this rubric was an industry standard."

Full draft: C-101: "Tool A achieved 75% accuracy, versus 50% for Tool B, in the 2026-08-15 training exercise" [E-01]. C-102: "Tool A was 25 percentage points better and therefore caused more accurate support answers" [E-01]. C-103: "Tool A is more accurate for all support teams and will improve customer satisfaction" [E-01]. C-104: "Tool A is used by 75% of organizations" [E-03]. C-105: "Tool A can create a first draft from a prompt" [E-04]. C-106: "Tool A's higher pass rate proves prior drafting experience was irrelevant" [E-02]. C-107: "Tool A achieved 75% accuracy [E-01]. Tool A causes more accurate answers [E-01]." C-108: "Tool A can create a first draft from a prompt. It is easier to use than Tool B" [E-04]. C-109: "Eight of the 12 Tool B participants passed" [E-01]. C-110: "The 10-item rubric is an industry standard" [E-05].

sections.title: Worked case: calculate, compare, and record decisions
paragraphs: Tool A's observed pass proportion is 9 / 12 = 0.75 = 75%. Tool B's is 6 / 12 = 0.50 = 50%. The absolute difference is 75% - 50% = 25 percentage points. The ratio is 75% / 50% = 1.5. The relative increase, using Tool B as the denominator, is (75% - 50%) / 50% = 0.50 = 50%. A difference of 25 percentage points, a ratio of 1.5, and a relative increase of 50% are different quantities. The report supplies no confidence interval, significance test, causal estimate, or basis for population-wide generalization.

C-101 audit row. Claim ID: C-101. Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES within the supplied evidence set. Identity matches: title, publisher, version, and date all match. Supporting passage: E-01 sentences one and two report 9 of 12 and 6 of 12. Support strength: DIRECT when "accuracy" is defined as meeting all 10 requirements. Scope matches: YES. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: KEEP.

C-102 must be split. C-102a: "The observed difference was 25 percentage points." Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: the two counts in E-01. Support strength: DIRECT after calculation. Scope matches: YES for this exercise. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: KEEP with the exercise scope. C-102b: "Tool A caused more accurate support answers." Citation/evidence_id: E-01 and E-02. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-02 says the nonrandom volunteer result does not establish causation. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. The design fails to establish causation, but that does not prove the opposite causal proposition. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE.

C-103 must be split. C-103a: "Tool A is more accurate for all support teams." Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-01 covers only 24 volunteers in one exercise. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED because the universal population claim was not tested. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE or replace with representative population evidence. C-103b: "Tool A will improve customer satisfaction." Citation/evidence_id: E-01 and E-03. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-03 says customer satisfaction was not reported. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED, not CONTRADICTS. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. The customer-satisfaction effect is UNKNOWN.

C-104 audit row. Claim ID: C-104. Citation/evidence_id: E-03. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-03 says the report contains no result for the number of organizations using any tool. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. Absence of an adoption measurement does not prove that the true adoption percentage is not 75%. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. Adoption is UNKNOWN. Establishing it would require an appropriate survey with a numerator, denominator, target population, sampling method, and date.

C-105 audit row. Claim ID: C-105. Citation/evidence_id: E-04. Resolves: PARTIAL because the copied fragment is available but the original page is inaccessible. Identity matches: title and publisher label are supplied; version and date are UNKNOWN. Supporting passage: the E-04 copied fragment. Support strength: PARTIAL because the fragment matches the sentence but its complete source context cannot be checked. Scope matches: QUALIFICATION NEEDED. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: copied plain text only. Action: REPLACE with an accessible first-party source or clearly label the statement unverified. Do not present it as independently verified.

C-106 audit row. Claim ID: C-106. Citation/evidence_id: E-02 and E-03. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four report fields match. Supporting passage: E-03, not E-02, says the association between prior drafting experience and passing was not estimated; E-02 explains the nonrandom design. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. Failure to estimate the association does not prove prior experience was irrelevant or that it mattered. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. The relationship between prior experience and passing is UNKNOWN.

C-107 contains two separately cited sentences. C-107a: "Tool A achieved 75% accuracy." Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: 9 of 12 passed. Support strength: DIRECT if accuracy is defined as the report's pass outcome. Scope matches: QUALIFICATION NEEDED because the sentence should name the exercise. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: QUALIFY. C-107b: "Tool A causes more accurate answers." Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-01 reports only observed counts, while E-02 says causation was not established. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES because each sentence already has its own citation. Action: REMOVE. Clear placement does not repair missing semantic support.

C-108 must be split. C-108a: "Tool A can create a first draft from a prompt." Citation/evidence_id: E-04. Resolves: PARTIAL. Identity matches: version and date UNKNOWN. Supporting passage: E-04 repeats this wording. Support strength: PARTIAL. Scope matches: QUALIFICATION NEEDED. Placement unambiguous: NO because one citation follows two claims and its boundary is unclear. Accessible alternative: copied plain text only. Action: REPLACE or qualify and place the evidence ID immediately after this sentence. C-108b: "Tool A is easier to use than Tool B." Citation/evidence_id: E-04. Resolves: PARTIAL. Identity matches: version and date UNKNOWN. Supporting passage: E-04 mentions drafting but contains no usability comparison. Support strength: BACKGROUND because the feature statement is related context but does not establish comparative ease of use. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: NO. Accessible alternative: copied plain text only. Action: REMOVE or replace with evidence from a defined comparative usability evaluation.

C-109 audit row. Claim ID: C-109. Citation/evidence_id: E-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-01 explicitly reports that 6 of 12 Tool B participants passed. Support strength: CONTRADICTS because the claim says 8 passed while the source reports the opposing count of 6. Scope matches: YES for the same participants and exercise. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REPLACE 8 with 6. This is a genuine contradiction, unlike an unmeasured quantity.

C-110 audit row. Claim ID: C-110. Citation/evidence_id: E-05. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: E-05 defines the local 10-item rubric and says the report did not evaluate whether it was an industry standard. Support strength: BACKGROUND because the passage gives relevant rubric context but does not establish industry-standard status. The missing evaluation is not proof that the rubric is not a standard. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE or replace with authoritative standards evidence. Industry-standard status is UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Worked case: repair the prose and handle uncertainty
paragraphs: Corrected publishable paragraph: "In one 2026-08-15 training exercise involving 24 volunteer support agents, 9 of 12 Tool A participants met all 10 locally defined rubric requirements, compared with 6 of 12 Tool B participants. The observed pass proportions were 75% and 50%, respectively, a difference of 25 percentage points. Using Tool B as the denominator, the relative increase was 50%." [E-01] "Participants were not randomly assigned, so the observed difference does not establish that Tool A caused better results. The finding applies only to the participants, task, and setting described in this exercise." [E-02]

The revision preserves the measured denominator, date, population, outcome definition, and setting. It does not claim production accuracy, customer satisfaction, organization adoption, industry-standard status, or causation. Those propositions remain UNKNOWN because the supplied evidence does not establish them.

Placement and semantic support remain separate. C-107 has clear sentence-level placement even though its second sentence is unsupported. C-108 has actual placement ambiguity because one evidence marker follows a feature claim and an unrelated superiority claim. Moving a citation can clarify attribution, but it cannot create support that the passage lacks.

If a relevant passage is inaccessible, record resolution as NO or PARTIAL as appropriate and mark unverified identity fields UNKNOWN. Do not use cached snippets as a substitute for the full source and do not request unauthorized restricted access. If two applicable sources explicitly report opposing counts or conclusions, preserve both passages and treat the disputed fact as UNKNOWN until a documented method resolves the conflict.

This process transfers to source material about Meta, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, and hosted assistants. For any provider, identify the exact model or product, version, date, plan, population, task, denominator, comparator, and outcome. A provider feature page can document a feature when identity and wording are verified, but it cannot by itself establish independent comparative superiority.

sections.title: Optional offline exercise: check audit record structure
paragraphs: This runnable standard-library Python exercise checks structure only. For the supplied exercise schema, it checks that the top-level value is a list, each row is a dictionary, required fields are present, claim_id and evidence_id are nonempty strings, enum values have the permitted shapes, claim IDs are unique, and supplied expected claim IDs have exact coverage. It permits the same evidence ID to support multiple claims. The implementation uses Python's isinstance, enumerate, set construction, set difference, str.strip, dict.get, and set.add operations as documented in the Python standard library: https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#isinstance, https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#enumerate, https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set, https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set.difference, https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.strip, https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict.get, and https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set.add. These record rules are supplied exercise requirements, not a claim that this is a universal audit standard.

Worked case: TASK-42-C1 uses evidence E-PY-1, resolves YES, has DIRECT support, and has action KEEP. TASK-42-C2 reuses E-PY-1, resolves PARTIAL, has PARTIAL support, and has action QUALIFY. The repeated evidence ID is allowed because claim IDs, not evidence IDs, must be unique. The independent changed-input task uses claim key TASK-42-C2-CHANGED and action REPLACE. Its expected-ID input changes to the same new key. The traceable structural decision is therefore that the changed record has exact expected coverage, while retaining the old expected key would produce both a missing-ID and an unexpected-ID error. These field values are audit decisions supplied to the checker, not decisions inferred by it.

The expected_claim_ids argument preserves the iterable contract. It accepts lists, sets, tuples, generators, iterators, and other iterable objects, but rejects a bare string, bytes value, dictionary, null, or non-iterable value. Python defines an iterable as an object capable of returning its members one at a time, normally through __iter__: https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-iterable. Because an iterator is exhausted after one full consumption, the checker converts expected_claim_ids to a list exactly once and then validates and reuses that same list for set construction. The relevant iterator and generator behavior is documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#iterator.__next__ and https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#generator-expressions. Positive generator and iterator fixtures protect this behavior, and a negative generator fixture verifies rejection of a non-string element.

The checker does not read evidence, calculate percentages, determine entailment, identify semantically unsupported claims, verify source identity, resolve live URLs, or grant access to restricted material. A structurally valid row can still contain a wrong semantic judgment. Its semantic correctness is UNKNOWN from this structural check alone. Calling check([]) without expected claim IDs returns no structural errors, but it does not certify completeness. Completeness is tested only when expected claim IDs are supplied. The checker is provider-neutral because it processes only ordinary Python values and does not call a model, provider API, network service, or non-standard package.

The fixtures include the original valid, evidence-reuse, worked-case, changed-input, duplicate-claim, missing-coverage, unexpected-coverage, malformed-top-level, malformed-row, list-valued-ID, missing-field, malformed-enum, and malformed-expected-ID cases. They also include positive generator and iterator coverage regressions, a negative generator-element case, and a non-iterable expected-ID case. Enum validation checks the value type before set membership, so list, dictionary, and null enum values produce ordinary validation errors. Assertions compare each result with an independently written expected result and compare the complete rendered transcript with the independently written EXPECTED_STDOUT constant. The stated output is derived from code inspection and fixture design, not from claimed execution during drafting.

Save the code as check.py and run it offline with python3 check.py. It uses only the Python standard library. Exact expected stdout:
valid fixture: []
evidence reuse fixture: []
worked case fixture: []
changed input fixture: []
generator expected IDs fixture: []
iterator expected IDs fixture: []
duplicate claim fixture: ['row 2: duplicate claim_id C-201']
empty coverage fixture: ["missing claim_ids: ['C-201', 'C-202', 'C-203']"]
unexpected coverage fixture: ["missing claim_ids: ['C-201']", "unexpected claim_ids: ['C-999']"]
malformed top fixture: ['records: expected list']
malformed row fixture: ['row 1: expected object']
list ID fixture: ['row 1: claim_id must be nonempty string']
missing fields fixture: ["row 1: missing fields ['action', 'evidence_id', 'resolves', 'support']"]
invalid enum fixture: ['row 1: invalid resolves value', 'row 1: invalid support category', 'row 1: invalid action']
enum shape fixture: ['row 1: invalid resolves value', 'row 1: invalid support category', 'row 1: invalid action']
null expected IDs fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: expected iterable of nonempty strings']
dict expected IDs fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: expected iterable of nonempty strings']
bare string expected IDs fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: expected iterable of nonempty strings']
list-valued expected IDs fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: elements must be nonempty strings']
generator element fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: elements must be nonempty strings']
non-iterable expected IDs fixture: ['expected_claim_ids: expected iterable of nonempty strings']

code.label: Offline structural checker with assertions and fixtures

sections.title: Independent changed-input task
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the answer key. It uses a new synthetic source set and changed counts. The report is titled "Notebook Assistant Pilot," published by the synthetic Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, dated 2026-09-01. Its scope is 20 students in two teacher-selected classrooms, with 10 students using Assistant X and 10 using Assistant Y during one 45-minute lesson. A response passed if it contained at least 4 of 5 required elements. This was a classroom exercise, not a production or long-term learning study.

N-01 identity: "Notebook Assistant Pilot," Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, 2026-09-01. Excerpt: "Assistant X: 8 of 10 responses passed. Assistant Y: 5 of 10 responses passed. The classes were selected by teachers and students were not randomly assigned. The lesson occurred once."

N-02 identity: "Notebook Assistant Pilot," Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, 2026-09-01. Excerpt: "The pilot found a higher pass proportion for Assistant X in this lesson. It did not measure long-term learning, student well-being, or performance in other classrooms."

N-03 identity: "Notebook Assistant Pilot," Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, 2026-09-01. Excerpt: "The report did not collect the number of schools using Assistant X. It contains no comparison with Assistant Z."

N-04 identity: "Assistant X feature note," publisher label Synthetic Assistant Publisher, version UNKNOWN, date UNKNOWN. Excerpt: "Assistant X supports response drafting." The original page is inaccessible; only this copied plain-text fragment is supplied.

N-05 identity: "Notebook Assistant Pilot," Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, 2026-09-01. Excerpt: "Assistant X had 8 passing responses and Assistant Y had 5 passing responses. Therefore, Assistant X had more passing responses than Assistant Y in this lesson."

N-06 identity: "Notebook Assistant Pilot," Synthetic Learning Lab, version 0.9, 2026-09-01. Excerpt: "The five-element classroom rubric was created for this lesson. The pilot did not assess whether the rubric predicts long-term learning."

Audit this draft: D-301: "Assistant X had 80% accuracy versus 50% for Assistant Y in the 2026-09-01 lesson" [N-01]. D-302: "Assistant X was 30 percentage points better, a 60% relative increase, and caused better learning" [N-01]. D-303: "Assistant X improves learning in schools" [N-02]. D-304: "Assistant X is used by 40% of schools" [N-03]. D-305: "Assistant X supports response drafting" [N-04]. D-306: "Assistant X's result proves teacher selection did not matter" [N-01]. D-307: "Assistant X had fewer passing responses than Assistant Y" [N-05]. D-308: "The five-element rubric predicts long-term learning" [N-06].

Split every compound claim before labeling support. For each atomic claim, record Claim ID, Citation/evidence_id, Resolves, Identity matches for title, publisher, version, and date, Supporting passage, Support strength, Scope matches, Placement unambiguous, Accessible alternative, and Action. Calculate both pass proportions, the percentage-point difference, the ratio, and the relative increase using Assistant Y as the denominator. Then write a corrected publishable paragraph. Mark unsupported measurements, generalizations, and causal claims UNKNOWN rather than guessing.

Graduated hints: Hint 1: start with 8 / 10 and 5 / 10. Hint 2: percentage points and relative increase use different calculations. Hint 3: N-02 and N-03 describe measurements that are absent, which calls for UNSUPPORTED rather than CONTRADICTS. Hint 4: N-04's wording is available, but its original identity and context are incomplete. Hint 5: nonrandom assignment does not prove whether teacher selection mattered. Hint 6: compare D-307 word for word with N-05 to find a genuine opposite-fact contradiction. Hint 7: N-06 is relevant background for the rubric but does not establish prediction.

sections.title: Independent practice answer key and feedback
paragraphs: Calculations: Assistant X passed 8 / 10 = 0.80 = 80%. Assistant Y passed 5 / 10 = 0.50 = 50%. The absolute difference is 80% - 50% = 30 percentage points. The ratio is 80% / 50% = 1.6. The relative increase, using Assistant Y as the denominator, is (80% - 50%) / 50% = 0.60 = 60%. A 60% relative increase is not a difference of 60 percentage points.

D-301 audit row. Claim ID: D-301. Citation/evidence_id: N-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: title, publisher, version, and date all match. Supporting passage: N-01 reports 8 of 10 and 5 of 10 in the lesson. Support strength: DIRECT if accuracy means passing the stated rubric. Scope matches: YES. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: KEEP.

D-302 must be split. D-302a: "The observed difference was 30 percentage points." Citation/evidence_id: N-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: the counts in N-01. Support strength: DIRECT after calculation. Scope matches: YES for this lesson. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: KEEP with scope. D-302b: "The observed relative increase was 60%, using Assistant Y as the denominator." Citation/evidence_id: N-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: the same counts. Support strength: DIRECT after calculation. Scope matches: YES. Placement unambiguous: YES. Action: KEEP with the denominator stated. D-302c: "Assistant X caused better learning." Citation/evidence_id: N-01 and N-02. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-01 describes nonrandom assignment, and N-02 says long-term learning was not measured. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. Neither passage proves an opposite causal effect. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. The causal effect on learning is UNKNOWN.

D-303 audit row. Claim ID: D-303. Citation/evidence_id: N-02. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-02 limits the finding to this lesson and says long-term learning and other classrooms were not measured. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED, not CONTRADICTS. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. Improvement in schools is UNKNOWN.

D-304 audit row. Claim ID: D-304. Citation/evidence_id: N-03. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-03 says the number of schools using Assistant X was not collected. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. Not collecting adoption data does not prove that 40% is false. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. The percentage is UNKNOWN because no numerator, denominator, school population, sampling method, or adoption date is available.

D-305 audit row. Claim ID: D-305. Citation/evidence_id: N-04. Resolves: PARTIAL. Identity matches: the supplied title and publisher label are available, but version and date are UNKNOWN. Supporting passage: the copied N-04 fragment repeats the feature wording. Support strength: PARTIAL because the original context cannot be inspected. Scope matches: QUALIFICATION NEEDED. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: copied plain text only. Action: REPLACE with an accessible first-party source or label the statement unverified.

D-306 audit row. Claim ID: D-306. Citation/evidence_id: N-01. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-01 says teachers selected the classes and students were not randomly assigned. Support strength: UNSUPPORTED. This design does not establish that selection was irrelevant, but it also does not prove that selection changed the result. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE. The effect of teacher selection is UNKNOWN.

D-307 audit row. Claim ID: D-307. Citation/evidence_id: N-05. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-05 reports 8 passing responses for Assistant X and 5 for Assistant Y and explicitly says X had more. Support strength: CONTRADICTS because D-307 says X had fewer. Scope matches: YES for the same lesson and groups. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REPLACE "fewer" with "more." This is a genuine contradiction based on an opposite reported fact.

D-308 audit row. Claim ID: D-308. Citation/evidence_id: N-06. Resolves: YES. Identity matches: all four fields match. Supporting passage: N-06 describes the lesson-specific rubric and says predictive validity was not assessed. Support strength: BACKGROUND because the passage is relevant to the rubric but does not establish prediction of long-term learning. The absent assessment does not prove that the rubric lacks predictive value. Scope matches: NO. Placement unambiguous: YES. Accessible alternative: supplied plain text. Action: REMOVE or replace with an appropriate validation study. Predictive validity is UNKNOWN.

Corrected publishable paragraph: "In one 45-minute classroom lesson on 2026-09-01, 8 of 10 Assistant X responses passed the lesson's 4-of-5-element rubric, compared with 5 of 10 Assistant Y responses. The observed pass proportions were 80% and 50%, respectively, a difference of 30 percentage points. Using Assistant Y as the denominator, the relative increase was 60%." [N-01] "Teachers selected the classes and students were not randomly assigned, so the comparison does not establish that Assistant X caused the difference. The result applies only to the two selected classrooms and this lesson." [N-01] No claim about long-term learning, school adoption, other classrooms, or predictive validity is published.

Common-error feedback: If you write 30% instead of 30 percentage points, you have confused absolute difference with relative change. If you write 60 percentage points, you have mislabeled the relative increase. If you claim better learning, you have substituted an unmeasured outcome for rubric passing and inferred causation from a nonrandom comparison. If you accept 40% school adoption, you have ignored the absent numerator and denominator. If you mark N-04 fully verified because its wording sounds plausible, you have confused plausibility with source identity and resolution. If you label D-303, D-304, or D-306 CONTRADICTS, you have treated missing evidence as proof of the opposite. D-307 is the genuine contradiction because N-05 explicitly reports the opposite ordering. D-308 is BACKGROUND because N-06 supplies relevant rubric context without establishing predictive validity.
